title: Google Wins Dismissal of Publishers' Lawsuits Over AI Overviews
key_facts: Judge Amit Mehta of the US District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed lawsuits by Penske Media and Chegg over Google's AI Overviews in a 30 Sep 2026 ruling.
The companies argued that letting Google index their content in return for visitors was an exchange that AI Overviews broke.
Mehta found no plausibly pleaded agreement: 'an expectation is not an agreement'.
The tying claim failed because he treated search and AI Overviews as one product, not two.
The ruling covers the antitrust claims only and does not decide whether Google may use copyrighted material.
ColombiaOne says reports differ on whether the Penske dismissal is without prejudice (can be refiled) or final and appealable.
Mehta said he is 'not unsympathetic' but that antitrust law cannot replace a legislature's judgment.
quote_evidence: But an expectation is not an agreement.
The decision does not establish that Google can use any copyrighted material it wants.
why_it_matters_hint: Publishers lose a main legal route against AI search summaries and the question of payment now shifts to Congress or licensing deals.
notes: ColombiaOne's article read first; WinBuzzer reports the same ruling in more detail and is credited as the source. Refiling uncertainty comes from ColombiaOne only.
